memo: Ours (new part, 10-24 plan audit): two-pipeline fusion. A = build.py base=f465 ownco=1 lfrag=1 (e3f465oc-1, LB 0.467, our best; base: sanpier 'Candidate-aware PubChem promotion 0.465' frozen pipeline = dmitriigluzdov v16 + sanpier fix, kernels/e3/base_f465.ipynb) and B = build.py base=v22 ownco=1 (e3v22ocg-1, LB 0.465; base: ahmedberatozer casmi26-v22-n1-challenger, kernels/e3/base_v22.ipynb), each with our own COCONUT table. Ours: a small orchestrator runs A then B as subprocess scripts (each with a glob filter so it sees only its own datasets, since both bases take the shortest file-name hit), cleans /kaggle/working between them, and fuses the two top-25 lists per molecule by reciprocal rank 1/(10+r) with equal weights (InChIKey14 keys; ties keep A's order). If B fails or would pass 8 h 35 min, the file is A's. Why: the two lines differ in the engine-1 FPNet (fold-safe vs full1), the NP / LOTUS priors and the PubChem promotion, and each scored within one molecule of the other, so their errors are partly independent. Effect size: expected top-1 change on 5-10% of molecules (logged by the kernel as 'top-1 changed vs A'). Run time: rerun budgets ICE 5400 + GLACIER 4000 + N1 1200 s per line, worst case about 6.9 h for both. Hypothesis: LB > 0.467 (gold 0.473 at rank 17 of 3,984 on 10-25). build_fu.py fu1 'base=f465 ownco=1 lfrag=1' 'base=v22 ownco=1'.
message: e3fu1-1: ours two-pipeline fusion (A = f465 + own COCONUT + lfrag, B = v22 + own COCONUT; reciprocal rank)
